title: Cherenkov Radiation in the Visible and Ultraviolet Spectral Ranges from 6-MeV Electrons Passing through a Quartz Plate
central_claims: UV/visible Cherenkov spectra are distinguished from pulsed cathodoluminescence for 6-MeV electrons traversing GE-014 and KU1 quartz.
Plate inclination strongly changes the extracted Cherenkov intensity and spectrum because total internal reflection constrains the collection geometry.

source_manifest.title: Cherenkov Radiation in the Visible and Ultraviolet Spectral Ranges from 6-MeV Electrons Passing through a Quartz Plate
source_manifest.finding: Russian original of the assigned English translation was read. Measured quartz spectra and output angles distinguish Cherenkov emission from cathodoluminescence; sapphire darkening and small diamond samples constrain other materials.

source_manifest.title: Investigation of Cherenkov Radiation Characteristics from 855 Mev Electron Beam
source_manifest.finding: Poster shares Potylitsyn and Vukolov. It explicitly uses the original angular relation in a rotated fused-silica radiator at MAMI, measuring beam profiles and comparing OTR. Nonideal focusing broadens both profiles.

source_manifest.title: Spectral and Amplitude–Time Characteristics of the Cherenkov Radiation upon Excitation of Transparent Materials by an Electron Beam
source_manifest.finding: Review by original authors reproduces the quartz spectral and angle findings, including collection limits. This is same-team synthesis, not independent confirmation.

source_manifest.title: Specific Features of Pulsed Cathodoluminescence under Excitation by Nanosecond and Subnanosecond Electron Beams
source_manifest.finding: Independent authors cite the original as one possible explanation for fast broadband emission reported elsewhere. Their narrow-band apparatus did not detect that component, so they neither reproduce nor falsify the 6-MeV quartz result.
